question: The layer made up of unconsolidated rock, dust, soil, etc. that is deposited on a bed rock surface like a blanket is known as
solution:
The Correct answer is __**Regolith**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Regolith** is a layer of loose, heterogeneous material covering solid rock.
 
• This layer includes **dust, soil, broken rock, and other related materials**.
 
• It is found on **Earth, the Moon, Mars, and some other celestial bodies**.
 
• The term **regolith** is derived from the Greek words "rhegos" (blanket) and "lithos" (rock).
 
• On Earth, regolith plays a significant role in **soil formation** and can be an essential factor in **ecosystem dynamics**.
 
• It also acts as a medium for **plant growth** and serves as a repository for **groundwater**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Talus**__

 __
 
• **Talus** refers to a pile of rock debris that accumulates at the base of a cliff, chute, or slope.
 
• It is typically formed by the mechanical weathering of rocks, such as through freeze-thaw processes.
 
 
 
• **Scree**__
 __
 
• **Scree** is a collection of broken rock fragments at the base of crags, mountain cliffs, or valley shoulders.
 
• Scree often forms through the action of gravitational forces.
 
 
 
• **Protolith**__
 
 
• **Protolith** is the original, unmetamorphosed rock from which a given metamorphic rock is formed.
 
• Identifying a protolith is essential in understanding the history and conditions of metamorphism.
